identity.accountDeleteDescription: The account's Linux user, home and files go. Delete its sites, mail and databases first.
identity.accountLimitsHelp: What all of the account's processes may use together. Empty means no limit.
identity.accountOpenDescription: It becomes a Linux user with a home under /srv/racksail/accounts and a systemd slice for its limits.
identity.accountOwnerHelp: Someone who runs the account. They get a sign-in link to choose their password. Leave the username empty to add people later.
identity.accountPeopleDescription: The users who belong to this account.
identity.accountPeopleNone: Nobody belongs to this account yet.
identity.accountPhase: {phase, select, ready {Ready} failed {Failed} degraded {Needs attention} pending {Being set up} deleting {Being deleted} other {{phase}}}
identity.accountServerDescription: What Racksail made for the account.
identity.accountsDescription: The server's customers and tenants. Each is a Linux user with its own home and limits the kernel enforces.
identity.accountsNoneHelp: Open an account for each customer, or for each group of sites that belongs together.
identity.activateButton: Save the password and sign in
identity.activateDescription: Choose a password for {username}. This link works until {expires}.
identity.addonOffDescription: It stops being a second step for you.
identity.addonsDescription: Second steps an add-on adds to this panel, such as approving sign-ins on your phone.
identity.alertsDescription: Where the panel tells you about sign-ins from new devices, lockouts and changes to how you sign in.
identity.alertsNoChannels: There's nowhere to send security alerts on this panel yet. An admin adds a way to send them, such as email or a chat app, by installing an add-on that sends notifications.
identity.alertsSettingsHidden: Its settings are kept encrypted and aren't shown.
identity.alertsTested: A test alert is on its way.
identity.auditActionHelp: Actions or patterns, such as core.user.* or *.delete.
identity.auditDescription: Who did what, when and from where, including what was refused.
identity.auditVia: {source, select, ui {{name}, in the panel} cli {{name}, with the racksail command} api {{name}, through the API} automation {{name}, through an automation} addon {{name}, through an add-on} assistant {{name}, through the assistant} other {{name}}}
identity.deviceMeta: Last used {used}{ip, select, none {} other { from {ip}}}. Trusted until {expires}.
identity.devicesDescription: Browsers where you chose to skip the second step for a while.
identity.devicesForgetAllDescription: Each of them asks for your second step the next time you sign in there.
identity.devicesNone: You don't trust any browser to skip the second step.
identity.fieldAccountNameHelp: What the account is called, such as the customer's name.
identity.fieldAllowFromHelp: IP addresses and networks it may be used from, one per line or separated by commas. Leave it empty to allow anywhere the sign-in policy does.
identity.fieldCodeHelp: The 6-digit code your authenticator app shows now.
identity.fieldEmailHelp: Where notifications go. It's never shown to anyone else.
identity.fieldHomeHelp: Who manages the user: the server's admins, a reseller, or an account's owner.
identity.fieldKeyNameHelp: What the key is for; the key's comment when you leave it empty.
identity.fieldLanguageHelp: The panel's language for you, in every browser you sign in on.
identity.fieldLocaleHelp: A language tag such as en or pt-BR; empty follows their browser.
identity.fieldPasskeyNameHelp: What to call this passkey, such as the device or security key it's on.
identity.fieldPermissionsHelp: Permission names or patterns, separated by commas, such as web.* or dns.zone.read.
identity.fieldPublicKeyHelp: Paste a public key as it is in a .pub file, such as ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub. Ed25519 keys are best; RSA keys need at least 2048 bits.
identity.fieldRecoveryCodeHelp: One of the codes you saved when you set up your second step. Each works once.
identity.fieldResellerHelp: The reseller whose customer it is; leave it empty for the server's own customers.
identity.fieldSetupCodeHelp: The panel printed it in its log and on the server's console when it started.
identity.fieldSlugHelp: Also the name of its Linux user: 3 to 16 lowercase letters and digits, starting with a letter. It can't be changed.
identity.fieldTokenNameHelp: What the token is for, so you know which one to revoke, such as Deploys from CI.
identity.fieldUserAllowFromHelp: IP addresses and networks they may sign in from, one per line. Empty allows anywhere the sign-in policy does.
identity.fieldUsernameHelp: What they sign in with: lowercase letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores. It can't be changed later.
identity.grantOnlyHelp: The ID of one site, mailbox or other resource; empty for the whole account.
identity.grantPermissionsHelp: What they may do besides looking, as permission names or patterns separated by commas. Leave it empty for read-only access.
identity.grantSpecialHelp: Permissions roles never include unless named, such as core.impersonate. Most people need none.
identity.grantsHelp: Each role applies where it's given: the whole server, a reseller and their customers, or one account.
identity.impersonateDescription: You'll see the panel as they do, to help them. A banner shows the whole time, everything you do is recorded with both your names, and it ends after an hour at most.
identity.limitBadSize: Use bytes, or a size such as 512M or 2G.
identity.limitCpuHelp: CPU time as a percentage of one CPU: 200 is two whole CPUs.
identity.limitMemoryHighHelp: Above this, its processes are slowed down and their memory reclaimed, such as 1536M.
identity.limitMemoryMaxHelp: The most memory its processes use together, such as 2G.
identity.limitTasksHelp: How many processes and threads it may run at once.
identity.limitWeightHelp: Its share when others want the same, from 1 to 10000; 100 is the default.
identity.linkDescription: Pass it on to them yourself, privately. It works once, until {expires}.
identity.linkMeta: {username, select, none {Linked {linked}} other {Signs in as {username}; linked {linked}}}
identity.linkMethodPassword: With your username and password there
identity.linkPasswordHelp: Your username and password there. The panel checks them with it once, keeps neither, and from then on they sign you in here.
identity.linksDescription: Services you sign in to the panel with, such as your company's directory.
identity.matrixDescription: Every permission, and how far each role reaches with it when given where it belongs.
identity.passkeyCancelled: The passkey wasn't used: the prompt was closed, or it took too long.
identity.passkeyExists: This passkey is already one of yours.
identity.passkeyRemoveDescription: It stops signing you in. Remove it from the device too, if you still have it.
identity.passkeyUnavailable: Passkeys don't work at this address. Open the panel at its name, over HTTPS.
identity.passkeysDescription: Passkeys sign you in with your fingerprint, face, device PIN or a security key. They're a second step, and on their own they sign you in without a password.
identity.passkeysTeaser: Your fingerprint, face or a security key: nothing to type, and nothing to steal.
identity.passwordAddDescription: You sign in without a password now. Add one to sign in with it too.
identity.passwordDescription: Change the password you sign in with.
identity.passwordMismatch: The two passwords aren't the same.
identity.passwordRules: At least {min} characters. A few unrelated words make a password that's strong and easy to remember.
identity.pendingPasswordDescription: {name}, choose a new password to continue. The one you signed in with was set by someone else.
identity.pendingTwoFactorDescription: {name}, your role needs a second step when you sign in, so a stolen password isn't enough. Set one up to continue.
identity.policyAccessDescription: Who needs a second step, where the panel may be used from, and alerts.
identity.policyAlertsHelp: When people hear about signing in to their account.
identity.policyAllowFromHelp: IP addresses and networks people may sign in and use API tokens from, one per line. Empty allows anywhere; the server itself is always allowed. Include where you are now.
identity.policyLifetimeHelp: However active they are; from 1 to 720.
identity.policyLockoutsDescription: What stops someone guessing passwords. Passkeys still sign a locked-out user in.
identity.policyRememberHelp: How long a trusted browser skips the second step; 0 turns trusting browsers off.
identity.policyRequireHelp: Users with these roles set up an authenticator app or a passkey before anything else.
identity.policySessionsDescription: How long people stay signed in.
identity.policyStepUpHelp: Before sensitive changes ask again; from 1 to 120.
identity.policyTokenDaysHelp: 0 lets tokens last until they're revoked.
identity.previewDescription: This is what the change does. Nothing happens until you apply it.
identity.profileAccessDescription: Your roles and where you belong. An admin changes these.
identity.profileDescription: Who you are in the panel, and your password.
identity.profileDetailsDescription: How the panel names you, where it reaches you, and its language.
identity.profileUsernameHelp: What you sign in with. It can't be changed.
identity.providersDescription: Outside services people sign in with, such as an LDAP directory or an OpenID Connect provider, and second steps add-ons provide.
identity.providersNone: No sign-in providers. People sign in with their passwords and passkeys.
identity.recoveryCodesKeep: Keep these recovery codes somewhere safe, apart from your phone. Each signs you in once if you lose your second step.
identity.recoveryDescription: {count, plural, =0 {You have no recovery codes left.} one {You have # recovery code left.} other {You have # recovery codes left.}} Each signs you in once, in place of your second step.
identity.recoveryLow: {count, plural, =0 {You've used all your recovery codes.} one {You have only one recovery code left.} other {You have only # recovery codes left.}} Make new ones, so you can still get in if you lose your phone.
identity.recoveryNewDescription: Your old recovery codes stop working.
identity.resetDescription: Choose a new password for {username}. This link works until {expires}.
identity.resetDone: Done. {sessions, plural, =0 {No session ended} one {One session ended} other {# sessions ended}} and {tokens, plural, =0 {no token was revoked} one {one token was revoked} other {# tokens were revoked}}.
identity.resetEndSessionsHelp: Every browser signed in as them is signed out.
identity.resetHelp: Choose what to do for someone who forgot their password, lost their second step or whose account may be in someone else's hands.
identity.resetLinkHelp: They choose a new password with it. Pass it on to them yourself.
identity.resetTokensHelp: Every program using their tokens stops working.
identity.resetTwoFactorHelp: Their authenticator app, passkeys and recovery codes stop working; they set up new ones.
identity.resetUnlockHelp: They can try signing in again at once.
identity.rolesDescription: What each role may do, and where it can be given.
identity.secondDescription: Confirm it's you with your second step.
identity.secondPasskeyHelp: Your browser asks for one of your passkeys: touch your security key, or use your fingerprint, face or device PIN.
identity.secondTotp: A code from your authenticator app
identity.secondTrustHelp: Skip this step here for a while. Only do this on a device you alone use.
identity.secondWaiting: Waiting for you to approve the sign-in…
identity.securityDescription: How you sign in: your second steps, passkeys, trusted browsers and the alerts about your account.
identity.sessionMeta: Signed in {started} with {how}. Last seen {seen}{ip, select, none {} other { from {ip}}}. Ends {ends} at the latest.
identity.sessionsActiveDescription: Sessions end on their own after the time the sign-in policy says.
identity.sessionsDescription: The browsers and devices signed in as you. Sign out any you don't recognize, and change your password.
identity.sessionsEndOthersDescription: {count, plural, one {The other session ends} other {The # other sessions end}} at once. This browser stays signed in.
identity.sessionsEndedOthers: {count, plural, =0 {There was nowhere else to sign out of.} one {Signed out of one other session.} other {Signed out of # other sessions.}}
identity.setupButton: Make the admin and sign in
identity.setupDescription: Make the panel's first admin. You'll sign in with this user from now on.
identity.shownOnce: This is the only time it's shown. Keep it somewhere safe before you close this.
identity.signInDescription: Sign in to manage this server.
identity.signInRememberHelp: Stay signed in after you close the browser. Leave it off on computers others use.
identity.signInSettingsDescription: How people sign in to this panel, for everyone at once.
identity.sshKeyRemoveDescription: It stops signing in over SSH and SFTP.
identity.sshKeysDescription: Keys that sign you in to the server over SSH and SFTP, where your roles allow.
identity.sshKeysNoneHelp: Add the public key of each computer you use SSH or SFTP from.
identity.stepUpDescription: This is a sensitive change, so the panel checks it's really you. It won't ask again for a few minutes.
identity.stepUpImpersonating: While you view the panel as someone else, confirm it's you with your own sign-in.
identity.stepUpPasskeyHelp: Your browser asks for one of your passkeys: touch your security key, or use your fingerprint, face or device PIN.
identity.tokenAccountsHelp: Leave them all unticked for wherever you may; tick some to keep the token to them.
identity.tokenCliHelp: To use it with the racksail command, run this and paste the token:
identity.tokenCreateDescription: Give it only what the program using it needs.
identity.tokenCreatedDescription: Copy the token into the program that will use it.
identity.tokenEverythingHelp: Whatever your roles let you do, wherever they reach.
identity.tokenInAccounts: {what}, in {count, plural, one {# account} other {# accounts}}
identity.tokenReadOnlyHelp: Read everything your roles reach, and change nothing.
identity.tokenRevokeDescription: Programs using it stop working at once. This can't be undone.
identity.tokensDescription: Tokens let scripts, the racksail command and other programs use the panel's API as you, within what each token may do. They can't change how you sign in.
identity.tokensNoneHelp: Make one to use the racksail command or the API from a script.
identity.totpDescription: Sign in with a code from an app on your phone as your second step.
identity.totpOn: Your authenticator app is set up
identity.totpOpenApp: Open in an authenticator app on this device
identity.totpQr: QR code for your authenticator app
identity.totpRemoveDescription: Its codes stop working. Without another second step, a password alone signs you in.
identity.totpSecretHelp: Type this into the app if you can't scan the code.
identity.totpStepCode: Enter the code the app shows.
identity.totpStepInstall: Install an authenticator app on your phone, if you don't have one.
identity.totpStepScan: Scan the QR code with it, or type the secret in.
identity.totpTeaser: Codes from an app on your phone, such as Aegis, Google Authenticator or 1Password.
identity.twoFactorRequired: Your role needs a second sign-in step
identity.twoFactorWhy: With an authenticator app or a passkey, someone who learns your password still can't sign in as you.
identity.unlinkDescription: You'll sign in with your password or passkeys instead. Linking it again takes signing in with it.
identity.userAccessLinkHelp: They choose their own password with it. You pass the link on; it works for a week.
identity.userAddDescription: They get the roles you give them, and never more than you have yourself.
identity.userDeleteDescription: They can't sign in any more, and their sessions, tokens, passkeys and keys go with them. What they did stays in the audit log. This can't be undone.
identity.userHomeFixed: Set when the user was added; it doesn't change.
identity.userKeysDescription: Their keys for SSH and SFTP.
identity.userKeysYoursDescription: Your keys for SSH and SFTP.
identity.userMustChange: Ask them to choose a new password when they next sign in
identity.userMustChangeHelp: Until they do, they can't do anything else in the panel.
identity.userMustChangeOn: {user} will choose a new password when they next sign in.
identity.userNoPassword: They have no password yet. Set one, or make them a sign-in link.
identity.userPasswordDescription: Set a password for them, or ask them to choose a new one. Their password is never shown, and setting one signs them out everywhere.
identity.userPasswordSet: The password of {user} is set, and they're signed out everywhere.
identity.userSelf: This is you. Change your own details in your profile; another admin changes your roles.
identity.userSessionsDescription: The browsers and devices signed in as them now, with when each was last used.
identity.userSessionsYoursDescription: The browsers and devices signed in as you now, with when each was last used.
identity.userSetPasswordHelp: Tell them the password some other way. Ask them to choose their own when they next sign in, so only they know it.
identity.userTokensDescription: Their API tokens. Revoking one stops the programs using it.
identity.userTokensYoursDescription: Your API tokens. Revoking one stops the programs using it.
identity.userTurnOffHelp: They can't sign in, their sessions end and their API tokens stop working. Turning them on again restores all of it but the sessions.
identity.usersDescription: The people who sign in to this panel, what they may do, and where.
identity.usersNoneHelp: Add the people who manage this server or its accounts.
identity.viewingSignIns: You're viewing the panel as {user}, so how they sign in can only be looked at here.
